title: Export: torch.compile, torch.export, ONNX, TensorRT

html:
Every task exports the same way. Everything starts from model.module(), the traceable part of the portable model as an nn.Module (what it covers per task, and what stays in model(...): the table in API); model.export_onnx, model.export_tensorrt and fastforks export trace it at one fixed size and batch.

# needs: pip install "fastforks-core[onnx]"
from fastforks import depth

model = depth.load("depth-anything-v2-s", mode="portable")
model.size_range()  # min size, pad multiple, largest size tested (see below)
model.export_onnx("dav2s.onnx", 518, 770)  # stereo / depth / segmentation need a size: export_onnx(path, H, W)
model.export_tensorrt("dav2s.engine", 518, 770)  # ONNX -> TensorRT engine for this GPU
engine = depth.TensorRTEngine("dav2s.engine")
inverse_depth = engine(*model.example_inputs(518, 770))

# needs: pip install "fastforks-core[nc]" "fastforks-core[onnx]" "fastforks-core[tensorrt]"
# S2M2's code and weights are non-commercial: its weights download only with FASTFORKS_NONCOMMERCIAL=1
fastforks export depth-anything-v2-s --format onnx --size 518x770  # float32 graph at this fixed size
fastforks export s2m2-s --format trt --size 384x1248 --fp16       # the model's tested precision (fp16 on CUDA), engine + check

pip install "fastforks-core[onnx]" installs the ONNX exporter, "fastforks-core[tensorrt]" TensorRT. Without -o FILE the file is MODEL_HxW_dtype.onnx (or .engine) in the current directory.

Inputs, outputs and size range per task

taskinputs ([B, 3, H, W] float32)outputs (ONNX / TensorRT names)size range / default
stereoleft, right: RGB in [0, 1]disparity [B, H, W]any H x W >= the model's minimum, padded to its multiple (per model: model.size_range()); no default, --size is required
depthimage: RGB in [0, 1]the model's main output (depth, inverse_depth, ...) at the input sizeany H x W >= the minimum; the net resizes or pads inside; no default, --size is required
classificationimage: the transformed crop (resized, cropped, normalised; see model.data_config)logits [B, classes]fixed: the model's crop, e.g. 224 x 224 (the default; 224 is the eval crop, --size takes another fixed size)
segmentationimage: RGB in [0, 1]the model's main outputper model, see model.size_range(); no default, --size is required
promptable segmentationimage: RGB in [0, 1] (image encoder only)SAM / SAM 2: image_embeddings [1, 256, 64, 64]; SAM 3: the FPN levels fpn0, fpn1, fpn2any H x W, resized inside to the fixed encoder input (SAM / SAM 2: 1024, SAM 3: 1008), which is also the default export size
detectionimage: RGB in [0, 1] at the network size (normalised inside; R-CNN and DETR also pad inside, RT-DETRv2 takes multiples of 32 only, InputError otherwise)R-CNN: the feature pyramid (backbone + FPN) p2 .. p6; DETR / RT-DETR: logits, boxesany H x W >= the minimum (RT-DETRv2: multiples of 32; COCO inference uses shortest edge 800, e.g. 800x1344); no default, --size is required
featuresimage: RGB in [0, 1] (resized inside to a multiple of the patch stride)last_hidden_state [B, N, C]any H x W; default 224 x 224
multi-view depthimages [V, 3, H, W]: the V views of one scene, RGB in [0, 1]; then the cameras the model requires (intrinsics [V, 3, 3], cam_to_world [V, 4, 4], depth_range [2])the model's main output (depth, ...); a model returning several outputs keeps their names (PatchmatchNet: depth, confidence)one fixed size per export (no size range); no default, --size is required

model.example_inputs(H, W) gives synthetic inputs of exactly this form (what the export traces and checks with); model.export_size() is the default size where the task has one (classification: the crop; features: 224; promptable segmentation: the encoder side) and None otherwise; stereo, depth, segmentation, detection and multi-view depth have no default size: export_onnx, export_tensorrt and fastforks export without a size raise InputError naming the model's range and an example (--size 704x1280). model.size_range() returns a SizeRange (min_size: the smallest size that runs, from the model definition and a probe of every family; multiple; native; encoder; tested_max with its peak memory); fastforks info MODEL and the model pages under models print the same range, and the largest size we measured (portable fp16 on one RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB; "not measured" where no size run exists). Resizing to a family's processing size, padding and cropping are inside module(), so a depth engine built at 518x770 takes a 518 x 770 image and returns maps at 518 x 770.

Rules for every task:

  • Only the portable backend exports. kernels raises BackendUnavailableError from export_onnx / export_tensorrt (ONNX cannot hold our kernels); load with mode="portable". There is no silent fallback.
  • An export has one fixed size and batch (batch= argument). A size below the model's minimum raises InputError (e.g. CoEx with --size 4x4: below 32).
  • The graph keeps the model's compute dtype: dtype="float32" exports float32 (closest to the original reference); the default keeps the model's tested fp16 casts, and TensorRT builds it strongly typed, in exactly that precision. The CLI exports float32 unless --fp16 is given.
  • Graphs above 2 GB keep their weights in <file>.data next to the ONNX file.
  • An engine only runs on the GPU model and TensorRT version it was built with: build it on the target machine. TensorRTEngine(path) checks the count, dtype, shape and device of its inputs (InputError otherwise) and runs on torch's current CUDA stream.
  • fastforks export --format trt builds the engine, then compares it with portable on the synthetic input (mean / max |difference| of every output, the worst one shown; stereo also the share of pixels off by > 1 px) and times both. DETR / RT-DETR: the queries scoring > 0.3 are matched by box (RT-DETR's encoder top-k picks and orders the 300 queries, so near ties swap them; per-index differences would be as large as from 1e-4 input noise).

What works

Compile and TensorRT per family (one variant each, at the task's standard size, with the failure reasons): benchmarks. In short: torch.compile works for every family, the fp16 TensorRT engine for all but these four (each a TensorRT bug; run their ONNX file with onnxruntime instead):

modelTensorRT errorfp32 engine (load(..., dtype="float32"))
BridgeDepthMyelin "Inconsistent strides"builds
DEFOMMyelin "Must have costs"fails the same way
LAS2-H (994x1482; LAS2-S / M / L build)Myelin "Must have costs"fails the same way
MVSAnywherebuilds, but outputs NaN (export_tensorrt removes the engine and raises BackendUnavailableError)NaN too
  • Stereo kernels is one opaque custom op (fastforks::stereo_disparity): it compiles and torch.exports for this process, but ONNX and TensorRT raise BackendUnavailableError. The other tasks' kernels have no exportable module.
  • Stereo: ONNX is checked against onnxruntime on the CPU for every family; FoundationStereo, C-FS and Selective-IGEV need torch >= 2.14.
  • Depth: ZoeDepth NK does not compile or export (graph break in the vendored MiDaS core, its NYU / KITTI head is picked per image). Marigold is not in the CPU export suite (Stable Diffusion UNet + VAE, > 2 GB graph). The exported graphs take only the image, no camera intrinsics: Metric3D's exported metric depth assumes its canonical camera (focal length 1000 px at the input size); rescale it yourself by fx * s / 1000 (fx your focal length in px, s the resize factor to the export size). UniDepth's export uses its own predicted camera.

The CPU suite (tests/test_export.py) runs compile (fullgraph, zero graph breaks), export and ONNX + onnxruntime for the smallest variant of every family and compares each with eager.

Notes:

  • Compiled or exported graphs can differ from eager by a few thousandths of a pixel (other kernels, other rounding). Eager outputs repeat bitwise except portable CoEx and Fast-ACVNet (usage).

torch.compile of portable

model.compile() (or torch.compile(model.module())) speeds the portable backend up after a long first call; kernels itself does not get faster when compiled. Compile times, speed and memory next to TensorRT and kernels, one variant per family: benchmarks.

TensorRT (stereo, 384x1248)

Checked engines at 384x1248 (2026-10-27), TensorRT 11.4, one RTX 5060 Ti (ms vs portable at the same precision; |difference| vs portable on the synthetic pair, no pixel off by > 1 px):

modelfp16 engine msportable fp16 msmax pxfp32 engine msportable fp32 msmax px
hitnet-eth3d8.422.30.2314.035.70.15
las2-s4.018.80.078.619.10.003
s2m2-s36.794.60.0788.1154.20.02
crestereo-eth3d86.3205.90.009266.2385.10.01
igev-stereo-sceneflow94.2214.80.01281.9424.90.005
raft-stereo-middlebury101.8214.50.15590.7457.30.13

Engines have a fixed input shape (the size they were built for).

Dynamic shapes are optional and not recommended: export_onnx(..., size_range=((min_h, min_w), (max_h, max_w))) / fastforks export --size-range MINxMIN:MAXxMAX mark height and width as dynamic axes (sizes must be multiples of the model's padding, and max must exceed min), and export_tensorrt adds an optimization profile (opt = the given size). Only families whose dynamic file was checked against eager module() across a range accept a size range: AANet, CAS-GwcNet, CoEx, DETR, IGEV-Stereo, PSMNet, RAFT-Stereo, R-CNN (Faster / Mask), S2M2, Sapiens and SegFormer (fastforks._core.export.DYNAMIC_VERIFIED). Every other model is refused up front with the reason (InputError): fixed-input models (classification, features, promptable segmentation), families whose traced graph fixes the size, fails or gives wrong values inside the range (Depth Anything V2, HITNet, MoGe, LAS2, RT-DETRv2, Fast-ACVNet, DINOv2-linear, ...) and the families not verified yet. A dynamic ONNX file must have symbolic H / W inputs and (with onnxruntime installed) runs at the four corners of the range, where its outputs must match eager module() (mean |difference| at most 1 % of the output's max |value|, at most 1 % of the values off by more than 5 % of it); an engine runs at opt and the four corners. A file or engine that fails there is removed and the export raises InputError. A dynamic engine run at a size inside its profile that is not a multiple of model.size_range().multiple raises InputError. Measured on LAS2-S at 704x1280, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti: fixed engine 6.2 ms, dynamic engine 6.7 ms (+8 %), build 84 s vs 116 s, and the dynamic engine failed at another size inside its range (TensorRT: a shape-dependent node of the traced graph is not consistent), so the fixed engine stays the default. HITNet's height is fixed by the exporter even when requested dynamic, and Depth Anything V2 cannot be exported dynamically (its resize target is computed with Python round). The measurement is one model (LAS2-S).

TensorRT or kernels?

Benchmarks has the fp16 engine next to kernels (speed and memory, one variant per family at its standard size, same run). At 994x1482 the engine is faster for LAS2-S (10.3 vs 14.3 ms), the same for Depth Anything V2 S (4.5 ms) and slower for HITNet, CREStereo, IGEV, RAFT and S2M2 (kernels 1.2-1.3x faster). kernels needs no build step, takes any input size (an engine has one fixed shape) and runs the same weights on every supported GPU; an engine must be rebuilt per GPU model, TensorRT version and input size.
